utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Morning, everyone. Wednesday the eighteenth. Can you all hear me, or am I talking to myself again?

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Yeah, got you. I was just saying, my weekend plans involve a long walk, apparently. Looking at the weather, it might be a very short walk to the pub.

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: Same here. We'd planned football at the weekend, but with this rain it'll be water polo. November, innit.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Lovely view of sideways rain from here. Very scenic.

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: Oh, and the charity bake sale on Friday. Just mentioning it, not volunteering anyone. Last year's brownies nearly needed a lifting plan.

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: Those were mine. Structurally sound, those brownies.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Right, before this becomes a structural engineering review of cake. Quick look back, then today's actual jobs.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: I signed off the inspection on the Line 3 Screw and Barrel on Tuesday. That's finished, not something we're carrying into today.

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: Yeah, saw the sign-off. Nothing outstanding on that one.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: And I already swapped the filter on the main water valve yesterday. That's done as well, before it gets read out twice.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Cheers. Finished filter job, understood. There's a risk assessment item for that valve, but that's separate.

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: Just an observation from nights: noticed the Forklift Fleet was running a bit warm, but it settled down.

utterances.speaker: Tomasz Nowak
utterances.text: Settled back to normal, you mean, or just stopped climbing?

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: Back to normal. No fault left on it. I'm not raising a repair job, just passing on what I saw.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: While we're on things that aren't moving, still waiting on parts for the Compressed Air Dryer. Nothing we can do until they arrive.

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: Yeah, that's the parts hold. No repair happening on that today as it stands.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Fine, blocked, not an extra job for someone to magic away. What have we got on the hydraulics?

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: I'll replace the seals on the Line 1 Hydraulic Power Unit by end of day.

utterances.speaker: Tomasz Nowak
utterances.text: Hang on, though—can't get to the line 1 hydraulics until production gives us a window. That bit hasn't changed.

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: Yeah, understood. I'll take the seal replacement, but I can't physically do it without that window. End of day is still what I'm aiming to deliver.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Okay, Jamie, agreed as yours by end of day, with production access still blocking the start. We're not saying you've got access when you haven't.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: That's how it reads, then. A commitment with an access dependency, not a booked stoppage.

utterances.speaker: Tomasz Nowak
utterances.text: And I'll do the pre-use checks on the forklifts by end of day.

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: Just so we're clear, end of day doesn't mean they can be used first and checked afterwards.

utterances.speaker: Tomasz Nowak
utterances.text: No, no. Checks before use, obviously. They're stood until they're checked. I'll have the checks done by end of day.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Thanks, Tomasz. Got that.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Tom, can you update the risk assessment for work on the main water valve by end of day? That one's safety critical, straight away.

utterances.speaker: Tomasz Nowak
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll update the risk assessment for work on the main water valve. Straight away on that one, and completed by end of day.

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: That's the assessment for the work, yeah. Not reopening yesterday's filter replacement.

utterances.speaker: Tomasz Nowak
utterances.text: Exactly. The risk assessment is what I'm taking. Safety critical, understood.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Good. That's the distinction I wanted.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: And the water booster filter? That's still on the list, isn't it? Not the one that was done yesterday.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: It is. I'll swap the filter on the water booster by end of day. It's urgent.

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: Right, Saz has the water booster, I've got the seals. Two different things, before my scribble merges them.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Your handwriting's doing its own resource planning again.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Marcus Hale, can you go to Kestrel Hydraulics Leeds to pick up the replacement parts for the feedwater pump by the end of the week? That one's safety critical, straight away.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: I can't take that, sorry. I can't leave the CHP plant for the collection. It'll need to be someone else.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Understood. Fiona, can you take that instead—go to Kestrel Hydraulics Leeds to pick up the replacement parts for the feedwater pump by the end of the week? Same priority: that one's safety critical, straight away.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll take it instead. I'll go to Kestrel Hydraulics Leeds and pick up the replacement parts for the feedwater pump by the end of the week. Safety critical, straight away, understood.

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: So end of the week is the completion limit, not a reason to leave the safety-critical one sitting until Friday?

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Exactly. Treat it as straight away, with the collection completed by the end of the week.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Thanks. Definitely handed over, then, rather than both of us thinking the other one's going.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Right, I'll run the monthly fire alarm test by 11am. Normal priority on that.

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: Sarah Okafor for the monthly fire alarm test, by 11am, normal priority. Got you.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Yep, that's mine.

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: Full name. Official now. Can't wriggle out of it.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Never could. Fiona, can you recalibrate the sensors on the air dryer by 11am? Normal priority.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll recalibrate the sensors on the air dryer by 11am. Normal priority, accepted.

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: Just separating those out—the sensor recalibration isn't the parts-dependent repair on the Compressed Air Dryer we mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Yep. I'm taking the recalibration, not claiming I can do the repair that's waiting on parts.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Correct. My blocked item stays blocked. No mystery delivery's turned up while we've been talking.

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: Um, I'll sort the training records for the new starters as well.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Thanks, Grace Liu. That's in the 'if you've got a spare minute' category, rather than another urgent one.

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll take it on that basis, if I've got a spare minute. No fixed deadline on the records.

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: A spare minute. Heard of those. Never seen one in the wild.

utterances.speaker: Grace Liu
utterances.text: Quite. Still, it's mine, just not jumping ahead of the safety-critical stuff.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Quick check before we finish: the production window is still the blocker on the seal replacement. Nothing said here removes that.

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: Yep. I've accepted the Line 1 Hydraulic Power Unit seals by end of day, subject to getting access. Not pretending otherwise.

utterances.speaker: Tomasz Nowak
utterances.text: And I've got the main water valve risk assessment, safety critical, straight away, by end of day. Plus the forklifts pre-use checks by end of day, before they're used.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: I've got the air dryer sensors by 11am, normal priority, and the feedwater pump parts collection by the end of the week, safety critical, straight away. Both accepted.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: And mine are the urgent water booster filter by end of day and the monthly fire alarm test by 11am, normal priority. That's the lot.

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: Nothing else from me. Even the rain's stopped for about four seconds.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: There you go. That's our weekend weather allocation used up.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Brilliant. Thanks, everyone. We'll leave it there.
